title: Cerulean Health - capacity roadmap & sovereignty checkpoint
next_steps: Redwood to share updated 24‑month commitment pricing and EU-onprem addendum (Maya) by 2026-08-03
Customer to provide 72-hour sample production request traces and 10 representative prompt templates (Amira) by 2026-08-02
SE-led latency benchmark with Cerulean prompt set in eu-west-1 and ap-southeast-1 (Ethan) scheduled week of 2026-08-09
action_items: Ethan Cole: run full P95/P99 latency bench with 512-token and 2k-token profiles against dedicated pool - due 2026-08-13
Maya Patel: send formal quote with two commitment tiers (12/24 months) and private deployment addendum - due 2026-08-03
Amira Khan: share sample request traces and ACL list for VPC setup - due 2026-08-02
Tom Reyes: confirm internal PO timeline and legal review window - due 2026-08-10
summary: Check-in to validate Cerulean's renewal appetite, scope a 24-month capacity uplift, and confirm data sovereignty path (EU-onprem pilot + hosted fallback). Discussed benchmarking, SLA expectations, and procurement timeline. Agreement in principle to pursue 2x committed capacity with EU private pilot before Q4.
topics: EU on-prem pilot and data residency
transcript:
[00:00:00] Maya: hey everyone, thanks for joining, we wanted to keep this one tight, 45 minutes, quick renewal & scale checkpoint. uh quick roll call?
[00:00:12] Lian: yep Lian here, hi. Amira?
[00:00:15] Amira: Amira here, sorry audio a tiny bit echoey on my end.
[00:00:18] Tom: Tom on procurement.
[00:00:20] Ethan: Ethan from Redwood SE, hi all.
[00:00:22] Maya: perfect. so high level, Cerulean's commitment comes up in October, we wanted to align on capacity needs, region add, and the EU sovereignty pilot.
[00:00:35] Lian: yes, timeline is right. our product team is targeting the new scheduling assistant for EU customers in Q4, so we need guaranteed capacity early Oct. main ask is: 2x current committed throughput, and data must be resident in EU for those flows.
[00:00:51] Amira: to add, we also need predictable P95 latency under 250 ms for the 512-token path. 2k token is allowed to be a bit slower, but P99 needs to be backstop'd.
[00:01:05] Ethan: okay that gives us concrete SLOs. quick clarifier - when you say "resident in EU" do you mean VPC-hosted private deployment or just region restriction on hosted?
[00:01:14] Lian: we prefer an on-prem or customer-managed VPC for the EU flows. legal is picky about the non-export of PHI-like telemetry, even though it's not PHI strictly.
[00:01:26] Maya: noted. our Private offering supports a customer-managed control plane; we can do an EU on-prem pilot with HSM/KMS integration. we'll need a short scoping doc and a network ACL list from Amira.
[00:01:40] Amira: okay I'll pull that. on the perf side, curious if you recommend dedicated GPU pools or a hybrid (dedicated primary with hosted fallback)
[00:01:49] Ethan: for predictable P95 at that token range, dedicated pools are best. hybrid is reasonable — dedicated as the primary path and hosted as overflow with automatic fallback. caveat: fallback means requests route to a compatible model variant; we can keep response format and behavior consistent but there can be subtle deltas.
[00:02:06] Tom: what's the impact on cost if we do hybrid? procurement needs ballpark numbers for budgets.
[00:02:11] Maya: we'll surface tiered pricing. rough rule of thumb: dedicated commitment reduces per-token effective cost by ~35% vs pure on-demand hosted. hybrid adds a small premium for the failover headroom. I'll attach a pricing sheet.
[00:02:24] Lian: can you also show the break-even if we do 12 vs 24 month?
[00:02:28] Maya: yes, two commitment tiers in the quote. 24-month gives stronger discounts and faster cadence for EU onprem activation.
[00:02:36] Amira: regarding security, do you support SAML/SSO, RBAC, audit logs shipping to our SIEM?
[00:02:42] Ethan: yes, SAML SSO is supported, RBAC is configurable, audit logs can be forwarded to your SIEM; for private/onprem we can integrate with your KMS or HSM for key custody. note sometimes the auto-transcript can say KMS as KMSA but it's KMS.
[00:02:58] Lian: (laughs) yeah that auto-stuff. wanted to call out one technical risk: our latency distribution is spiky during peak scheduling windows. we rely heavily on prefix caching because many patients queries start the same way. how does Redwood handle prefix caching and KV cache consistency?
[00:03:14] Ethan: good point. we do prefix/KV caching at the serving runtime — it stores common prefixes in memory and reuses KV cache across requests when safe. consistency is preserved; invalidation can be manual or TTL based. small caveat: on fallback to hosted the cache won't be shared, so cold-starts for those requests can be noticeable unless we pre-warm.
[00:03:33] Amira: pre-warm — is that something you can automate for a rollout?
[00:03:36] Ethan: yes, we have scripts and can run warm-up waves to populate caches and KV for your prompt templates before cutover. we'll include that in the runbook.
[00:03:45] Tom: on procurement cadence — legal needs a SOC 2 attestation and vendor questionnaire answered. do you have the security pack?
[00:03:52] Maya: yes, we have the security kit. I'll drop the SOC 2 report, ISO artifacts, and the vendor questionnaire answers. for private we can also provide network diagrams and third-party test results.
[00:04:03] Lian: thanks. if we do EU onprem pilot, what's the typical activation timeline?
[00:04:09] Ethan: from signed SOW to pilot activation typically 8-10 weeks. less if there's already infra alignment at your end. the SOW includes milestones: network runway, KMS integration, bench, canary, cutover.
[00:04:21] Amira: 8-10 seems tight for our legal and change control, but doable if procurement pushes.
[00:04:26] Maya: that's where the hybrid helps — we can ramp hosted capacity quickly while the onprem pilot progresses. so Oct go-live for EU flows could be on hosted then cutover to onprem in November if timelines slip.
[00:04:38] Lian: ok. what about model variance? we use a tuned open model right now — will fallback change outputs?
[00:04:45] Ethan: small differences possible; we recommend pinning a model family and using rollout policies to route to a compatible quantized variant if capacity becomes constrained. Redwood Optimize can surface quality regressions using your eval prompts.
[00:04:58] Amira: that Optimize product — will it run our eval sets and alert on regressions?
[00:05:02] Ethan: yes, you can upload prompt/eval sets. it reports token-level cost implications, and alerts when generation quality drifts vs baseline.
[00:05:10] Tom: back to numbers — can we agree in principle to 2x capacity for the 24-month term subject to benchmarks and legal?
[00:05:16] Lian: yes, in principle. need to see the numbers and the bench.
[00:05:20] Maya: great, so agreed in principle. we'll put together a formal quote with two options: a 12-month and a 24-month, both with EU-onprem pilot addendum and a hybrid fallback plan. action items we'll track.
[00:05:33] Amira: a couple of technical asks for the bench: include 512-token conversational, 2k-token longform, and a bursty arrival pattern; also please simulate our peak 120 RPS burst.
[00:05:44] Ethan: noted — we'll mirror that. any latency bucket requirements beyond P95 250 ms?
[00:05:49] Amira: P99 should be < 1.1s for 512, and warm-cache P95 < 200ms if possible.
[00:05:56] Ethan: okay we'll capture those.
[00:05:58] Tom: procurement timeline — I'm aiming to have internal approval by Aug 18, legal review complete by Aug 31.
[00:06:05] Maya: good call. we'll try to hit the 2026-08-03 quick quote delivery.
[00:06:09] Lian: any blockers re: compliance for the pilot?
[00:06:12] Ethan: only the usual: KMS integration, SOC2 artifacts. for onprem we do need network ACLs and service account details. nothing unusual.
[00:06:22] Amira: I'll share a minimal ACL and the list of IP ranges.
[00:06:26] Maya: perfect. to recap — agreed: pursue 2x committed capacity with a 24-month preferred option; Redwood to deliver pricing, SOW template, security pack; SE to run bench and share results; customer to supply traces and ACLs.
[00:06:39] Lian: sounds good. one small note — we sometimes see product names morph in the transcript (for example, dedicated called 'dedi-cated' by the bot) so apologies if some words are odd in these notes.
[00:06:49] Maya: no worries — that's expected. okay let's capture next steps and close. thanks all.
[00:06:56] Ethan: thanks everyone.
[00:06:58] Tom: bye.
[00:07:00] [meeting ended]
references: Note: SE will upload benchmark script and raw runs to shared folder after bench complete
